question: What is the main goal of primary prevention in cardiovascular care?

options.A: To manage sudden cardiac arrest inside the emergency room
options.B: To screen individuals who already have high blood pressure
options.C: To treat established heart failure and reduce disability
options.D: To stop the disease before it starts in healthy people

explanation: Primary prevention targets healthy individuals to prevent the initial development of cardiovascular disease through health promotion and risk reduction. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h1)

question: A patient with a history of a previous heart attack is receiving counseling on diet and taking prescribed statins. Which level of prevention does this care represent?
explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early diagnosis, prompt medical treatment, and lifestyle changes to halt disease progression in someone who already has a condition. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h1)

question: Which of the following is a modifiable cardiovascular risk factor?
explanation: Blood pressure can be modified through diet, exercise, and medication, whereas age, sex, and genetics cannot be changed. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h2)

question: Why does a family history of early-onset heart disease increase a patient's cardiovascular risk?

options.A: It indicates shared genetic predispositions and sometimes similar unhealthy home environments
options.B: It means the patient's body cannot physically process physical exercise
options.C: It guarantees that the person will develop high cholesterol by age thirty
options.D: It completely prevents any positive effects from lifestyle modifications

explanation: Genetics play a strong role in lipid metabolism and vascular health, and family members often share dietary and lifestyle habits that compound risk. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h2)

question: What is the primary reason for recommending a low-sodium diet in cardiac prevention?

options.A: It prevents the liver from producing too much cholesterol
options.B: It reduces fluid retention and lowers blood pressure
options.C: It stops the pancreas from releasing excess insulin
options.D: It increases the amount of dietary fiber in the gut

explanation: Excess sodium holds extra fluid in the blood vessels, increasing the pressure against arterial walls and forcing the heart to work harder. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h3)

question: A patient asks why eating soluble fiber helps protect their heart. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Fiber burns off extra calories before they turn into body fat
options.B: Fiber binds to cholesterol in your digestive tract so your body removes it
options.C: Fiber directly opens up tight blood vessels to improve circulation
options.D: Fiber replaces all the salt in your meals so your kidneys can rest

explanation: Soluble fiber binds with cholesterol-containing bile acids in the intestine, preventing their reabsorption and promoting their excretion in stool. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h3)

question: How many minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise are generally recommended per week for cardiovascular health?
explanation: Standard health guidelines recommend a minimum of 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly to maintain heart health and lower disease risk. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h4)

question: Why is regular aerobic exercise considered beneficial for a patient's lipid profile?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for dietary changes
options.B: It permanently lowers resting body temperature
options.C: It stops the liver from producing red blood cells
options.D: It helps raise HDL cholesterol levels to clear out arterial plaque

explanation: Aerobic exercise is one of the most effective lifestyle interventions for increasing HDL, the 'good' cholesterol that transports lipids away from arteries. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h4)

question: Which component of cigarette smoke reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood?
explanation: Carbon monoxide binds tightly to hemoglobin in red blood cells, pushing out oxygen and reducing the amount of oxygen delivered to the heart and other tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h5)

question: A patient states they have smoked for twenty years and wonders if quitting will even help now. What is the most accurate nursing response?

options.A: Smoking only affects your lungs, not your heart or blood vessels
options.B: You must stop all at once without any help or replacement products for it to work
options.C: Quitting will benefit your heart immediately, cutting your heart disease risk in half within one year
options.D: The damage is already permanent, so quitting will not change your risk level

explanation: Cardiovascular benefits begin almost immediately after quitting smoking, and within twelve months, the excess risk of coronary heart disease drops by fifty percent. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h5)

question: Why are hypertension and dyslipidemia frequently referred to as silent conditions?

options.A: They disappear completely on their own without treatment
options.B: They rarely cause noticeable symptoms until severe damage occurs
options.C: They only occur in patients who cannot speak
options.D: They cannot be detected using standard medical equipment

explanation: High blood pressure and high cholesterol develop gradually over years without outward warning signs, making regular screening mandatory. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h6)

question: Which nursing action helps ensure an accurate blood pressure reading during a screening clinic?

options.A: Using a cuff that is much smaller than the patient's arm circumference
options.B: Allowing the patient to chat actively while the cuff inflates
options.C: Taking the measurement immediately after the patient jogs up the stairs
options.D: Ensuring the patient's arm is supported at heart level with feet flat on the floor

explanation: Proper positioning prevents muscle tension and gravitational artifacts that can falsely raise blood pressure readings. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h6)

question: How does chronic psychological stress directly impact the cardiovascular system?

options.A: By forcing the body to store extra vitamins in the heart muscle
options.B: By lowering resting heart rate to dangerous levels below forty beats per minute
options.C: By improving the elasticity of large arteries through natural relaxation
options.D: By keeping stress hormones elevated, which raises blood pressure and inflammation

explanation: Prolonged stress floods the body with adrenaline and cortisol, raising blood pressure, increasing heart rate, and promoting inflammatory changes in blood vessels. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common unhealthy coping mechanism associated with high chronic stress?

options.B: Turning to tobacco use or excessive smoking
options.C: Adopting poor dietary habits and overeating
options.D: Withdrawing from social and physical movement

explanation: Regular physical exercise is a healthy stress management tool, whereas smoking, poor diet, and physical withdrawal are unhealthy responses to stress. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of using the teach-back method during patient education?

options.A: To test if the patient can read a complex medical textbook
options.B: To force the patient to memorize their medication schedule word for word
options.C: To have the patient explain the instructions back in their own words to verify understanding
options.D: To give the nurse a break from talking during discharge planning

explanation: Teach-back allows nurses to confirm comprehension and correct any misunderstandings before the patient leaves the clinical setting. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h8)

question: A community health nurse wants to help lower the rate of undiagnosed high blood pressure in a low-income neighborhood. Which activity is the best initial approach?

options.A: Mailing complex research journals to every household in the area
options.B: Instructing residents to buy their own digital blood pressure monitors online
options.C: Waiting inside the hospital clinic for patients to schedule appointments
options.D: Setting up a free mobile blood pressure screening booth at a local community center

explanation: Community outreach brings screening services directly to populations with limited healthcare access, enabling early detection of silent conditions. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h8)
